trigger: any CI test phase on this branch
policy_floor: broken test leg introduced by this change
classification_rationale: the row pushed the file past an enforced 32,000-char budget; tests/test_issue_docs.py failed
summary: routed-concern row exceeded the 32,000-char instruction-file budget (separate from the 40,000 hard cap), failing tests/test_issue_docs.py. Fixed by moving the four catastrophic clauses into the routed doc and leaving a pointer row. Gate 1's claim of a green full surface was true pre-merge and false at the reviewed HEAD.

trigger: sidecar write or rename fails during a re-upload of a signed package
classification_rationale: header promised the package is left honestly unsigned; the previous sidecar survived
summary: a failed replace removed only the staging file, leaving the PREVIOUS signature over bytes that no longer existed - refused by every anchored agent in both modes. Found independently by cpp-safety and security-guardian. Both failure paths now discard the predecessor; pinned by a test using a realistic failure injection.

trigger: a zero-byte <binary>.sig in the update directory
classification_rationale: the Signed column claimed to make the same decision as CheckForUpdate; for a zero-byte file it did not
summary: a zero-byte sidecar returned kServed: the column said signed, the wire field was empty, and the agent read empty as ABSENT and applied the binary UNVERIFIED in permissive mode. Now refused. severity_native MEDIUM per the reporter; derived BLOCKING and the derived band governs.

trigger: unprivileged local user creates update-trust-bundle.pem before the operator provisions it, on a Windows host configured to use that path
classification_rationale: the comment and the operator docs both claimed the ACL kept unprivileged users out; Inno [Dirs] Permissions adds ACEs and cannot break inheritance
summary: Inno's [Dirs] Permissions cannot disable inheritance, so %ProgramData%'s inherited rights would allow an anchor plant. An icacls /inheritance:r [Run] step now enforces it and both false claims are corrected. NOT verified on Windows - MSVC CI is the enforcement point.

trigger: a failed exists() on the sidecar's parent (EACCES/EIO)
classification_rationale: a failed existence check silently became 'absent', i.e. unsigned
summary: a FAILED exists() returned kAbsent, so an unreadable parent read as 'unsigned' with no log; under --update-require-signature the fleet then refuses with no server-side cause. Now kUnreadable.

trigger: an oversized or /dev/zero-symlinked <plugin>.sig
classification_rationale: the lift replaced a streaming read with an unbounded slurp
summary: the plugin signature read lost its implicit bound when the verifier was lifted. Capped at the shared kMaxSignatureBytes, which now lives in the shared header.

trigger: a fourth refusal reason added in updater.cpp
classification_rationale: producer and consumer kept separate hardcoded reason lists
summary: the heartbeat summed a hardcoded reason list, so a new reason would be counted by neither the tag nor the fleet gauge. Both sides now iterate one shared constant.

trigger: operator greps the agent log for the documented error string
classification_rationale: the documented string cannot be emitted by this code path
summary: the docs told operators a missing intermediate fails with 'unable to get local issuer certificate'; CMS reports 'certificate verify error'. Verified by reproducing through drain_openssl_errors. Corrected.

trigger: operator follows the Windows enablement row
classification_rationale: setx /M is not visible to a merely-restarted service
summary: services inherit their environment from services.exe, cached at boot, so the documented setx route would leave the bundle unset and verification silently OFF. Now prefers the binPath route and says why.

trigger: upload a package whose filename ends .sig
classification_rationale: required-doc item 1: a changed error path on a documented endpoint
summary: the new .sig filename rejection (400) was documented nowhere. Added to the upload procedure.

trigger: operator upgrades to a release carrying this change
classification_rationale: required-doc item 2: an upgrade step; the sibling plugin-signing feature has one and is not breaking
summary: no upgrade note. Adjudicated against release-deploy, who argued Upgrade Notes is breaking-only: '### vNEXT - Plugin code signing (#80)' carries no breaking label, so the precedent holds. Note added, which also discharges the undocumented-sidecar-artifact finding.

trigger: an engine principal or agentic worker tries to upload a signed package or read signing state
classification_rationale: ADR-1005 requires a versioned REST and MCP twin or a recorded exception
summary: signature upload and signed-state read are reachable only through the dashboard; no /api/v1 twin, no MCP tool, no exception-ledger entry. The /api/settings prefix is accepted precedent for the OTA capability as a whole - the finding is the absent versioned twin. To be filed as a follow-up issue.

trigger: any render of the updates settings fragment
summary: the Signed column read up to 64 KB per package purely to discard it. An outcome-only entry point now delegates to the same decision without the read.

trigger: a member inserted before signature_trust_bundle
classification_rationale: positional aggregate init of the fail-open guard
summary: main.cpp built UpdateConfig positionally while agent.cpp used designated initialisers. Now designated on both.

trigger: an include reorder dropping the transitive path
summary: added a direct <cstdio> include.

trigger: a future regen dropping field 7 from the codec
classification_rationale: maps:get/3's default made the case pass if the field were dropped
summary: the absent-signature case supplied a default, so it could not discriminate the regression the module exists to pin. Now maps:get/2.

trigger: deleting X509_STORE_set_purpose entirely
classification_rationale: the test comment overstated what the case pins
summary: measured: deleting the purpose line still fails this case via OpenSSL's own smime_sign default; what it actually discriminates is the purpose being WEAKENED. Comment corrected to say so.

trigger: operator follows the metrics.md link
classification_rationale: link text pointed at a different section's anchor
summary: anchor corrected, and the gauge row now states it counts only endpoints currently reporting heartbeats.

trigger: ISCC compiles yuzu-agent.iss during the release workflow (release.yml:704)
policy_floor: broken platform build leg introduced by this change
summary: the icacls [Run] entry was spliced INTO the [Dirs] section, because a python s.replace('[Run]',...) anchor matched the literal '[Run]' inside a comment written in the same edit; an orphaned sentence fragment was left as a bare directive line. [Dirs] accepts no Filename/Parameters/StatusMsg. No PR-CI leg parses this file - release.yml is the only place it is compiled - so it would have failed at release. Rebuilt the [Dirs] block and re-anchored the [Run] entry on a unique two-line anchor; structural validation reports 0 errors.

trigger: a malicious or impersonated update server serves a genuinely-signed OLD agent binary with latest_version='99.0.0' and sha256 recomputed over those same bytes
summary: FALSE ASSURANCE (I6a). The header conceded the signature binds no version, then claimed the updater supplies that binding 'with the server-supplied SHA-256 and the semver downgrade check' - both authored by the very server the signature exists to distrust, so neither defends against a rollback. Every agent-side check passes and the endpoint installs a known-vulnerable signed build reporting itself current. NOT closed in code: closing it requires binding the version into the signed material (a signed manifest, TUF-style), which changes the release-signing format. Resolved as the reviewer directed - by making the claim truthful at every surface an operator or maintainer reads (header, server-admin.md, changelog fragment): this closes SUBSTITUTION, confining an attacker to binaries the key has signed, and does not close ROLLBACK. Follow-up issue filed for the manifest-signing design.

trigger: on Windows a concurrent CheckForUpdate holds the sidecar open without FILE_SHARE_DELETE, so the rename fails with a sharing violation during an ordinary signed re-upload
adjudication_rationale: supersedes the gov-b2 remediation, which was correct about the availability symptom and wrong about the direction of the fix
summary: THE gov-b2 FIX WAS WRONG IN DIRECTION. Making failure discard the predecessor turned a benign, common Windows failure into silently STRIPPING a valid signature, after which permissive agents apply the new binary UNVERIFIED. Enumerating the windows settles it: old-binary+new-sig and new-binary+old-sig both fail CLOSED; new-binary+NO-sig is the only unsafe state. Deleting a signature is therefore only ever an operator's explicit choice to upload unsigned, never a failure recovery. gov-b2's real concern (an undeliverable package) is now met by REPORTING the partial failure to the operator instead of by destroying the signature. Test inverted and mutation-probed: restoring the delete fails it (2 assertions).

adjudication_rationale: mechanism replaced, not the finding released; band and gate unchanged
summary: SUPERSEDED MECHANISM (see gov-b7). The original fix - discard the predecessor on failure - was itself a security defect. The finding stands and is still fixed, but by surfacing the partial failure to the operator (HX-Trigger error toast + an error log naming the package as not deliverable) rather than by removing the signature.

trigger: the binary is written and the signature sidecar write or rename then fails
summary: the failure was logged server-side and the operator was served an ordinary success fragment, so an upload that left the package undeliverable read as a completed one. Now surfaced with the file's own established idiom (HX-Trigger showToast error), with the fragment still rendered at 200 so the table shows the REAL on-disk state.

trigger: n/a - cosmetic or doc-precision
summary: kMaxSignatureBytes was documented as 'shared by both callers'; grep shows plugin_loader.cpp is its only consumer. The OTA wire signature is bounded by the SERVER's own same-named constant plus the gRPC frame limit - different binaries, no shared header, equal value incidental. Comment corrected and the independence stated so neither is cited as enforcing the other.

trigger: n/a - cosmetic or doc-precision
summary: the unsigned tooltip read 'No signature stored', false for over-cap, unreadable and zero-byte sidecars, which ARE stored but unservable - pointing the operator at 'upload one' when the fix is 'fix the one there'. Re-worded to 'No usable signature is being served' with the causes enumerated.

trigger: n/a - cosmetic or doc-precision
summary: 'untrusted' was documented as a closed set of two causes; the code maps a THIRD - an unreadable or missing trust bundle - onto the same label. That is the most likely operator misconfiguration and was absent from the label's documented meaning. Added, and flagged as the first thing to check when the counter jumps after a config change.

trigger: n/a - cosmetic or doc-precision
summary: a corrupt-but-well-sized sidecar was the one state every surface called servable and nobody validated: stored, column says signed, server serves it, every anchored agent refuses in BOTH modes - including permissive, whose documented contract is that unsigned packages are accepted with a warning. Added a pure PEM-CMS shape check (looks_like_pem_cms) accepting both CMS and PKCS7 armour and requiring a matching footer, placed AHEAD of the binary write so a rejection leaves the previous package and signature untouched. Mutation-probed: reducing it to a header-only sniff fails 3 assertions.

trigger: n/a - cosmetic or doc-precision
summary: 'missing' was named among reasons appearing in the endpoint's own log; it is a metric label only - the emitted line is 'update package is unsigned and --update-require-signature is set'. Adjacent to a passage telling operators which literal strings to grep. Corrected.

trigger: n/a - cosmetic or doc-precision
summary: the signature file input used class 'form-row' among 'mini-field' siblings in the same inline row - the stacked full-width variant, which breaks the row's layout.

trigger: an API-only principal needs the OTA signing surface
refutation_evidence: docs/adr/1005-*.md frontmatter is 'status: proposed', and its Binding-status paragraph states: 'Nothing in this ADR binds reviews or blocks PRs until its status is accepted.' A proposed ADR is not an accepted ADR, so it is not one of the three closed sources of a policy floor.
adjudication_rationale: clears policy_floor; the finding's merits survive as tracked debt rather than as a gate. On the merits it WOULD be a real Decision-4 miss (an HTML fragment endpoint is UI and does not satisfy the rule), but the whole OTA capability is dashboard-only today, not just this change - so it is a pre-existing capability-wide gap, not one this diff introduces.
summary: REFUTED AS A GATE, retained as debt. Follow-up issue filed for the REST/MCP twin covering the OTA capability as a whole.
